key_insight: TrackEverything reframes video tracking as a 3D world problem instead of a 2D frame-by-frame problem, enabling dense tracking over long time horizons. By maintaining persistent scene tracks in world coordinates, it removes the usual tradeoff between tracking many points and tracking for a long duration.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the long-standing limitation in point tracking systems that force a choice between sparse long-range tracking and dense short-range tracking. It aims to make dense tracking scalable across entire videos without losing track consistency over time.
method: Represents video observations as persistent 3D scene tracks in world coordinates rather than short-lived 2D trajectories.
De-duplicates repeated observations of the same physical points across frames to keep the representation compact and stable.
Decouples model complexity from video length, allowing the tracker to scale to longer horizons while still handling dense point sets.
impact: This matters because it enables more practical and reliable tracking for robotics, AR/VR, video understanding, and 3D reconstruction, where both density and long-term consistency are important. Practitioners gain a way to track many points across long clips without the typical accuracy or memory tradeoffs.

paper_title: TrackEverything: Long Horizon Dense Tracking via De-Duplicating 3D Scene Representations
paper_authors: Ayush Jain, Sreeharsha Paruchuri, Ishita Gupta, Fan Zhang, Tanner Schmidt
